newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Hillsdown sees pickup despite BSE.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Hillsdown sees pickup despite BSE.

text.p: British food group Hillsdown Holdings swung into profit at the halfway stage on Thursday and chairman Sir John Nott said he was hopeful about the outlook for the rest of 1996.

"There is a long way still to go but, subject to the fourth quarter on which a great deal depends, we see no reason why the current encouraging trend should not extend to the full year," said Nott, a former minister of defence.

Hillsdown, marmalade, tea and chocolate biscuits, reported a pretax profit of 43.7 million pounds ($68.5 million) in the six months ended June 30 after a loss of 68.1 million last time due mainly to the sale of Maple Leaf Foods in Canada.

"The outloook for 1996 is promising. Apart from problems caused by the BSE crisis in some companies, our food, furniture and housebuilding operations are trading rather more successfully than over the past year or two," said Sir John.

The scare over the possibility that madcow disease -- bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) -- in cattle might be spread to humans had hurt Hillsdown's meat business, but helped its poultry and fish sales which remain strong.

Hillsdown's meat and produce business trading profits fell to 4.3 million pounds, from 7.6 million in the first half of 1995, but Nott said its furniture companies had responded well to strong consumer demand.
Its furniture and housebuilding businesses turned in operating profits of 16.3 million pounds in the period, up from 13.4 million last time.
